argument:
Fix to the desk's finding. Round 1's first target (158.83) paid 0.647R gross (desk_r1.json) because there is no real ceiling between my entry area and today's high 158.847. I cannot get 1.5x to a target under 158.85 without a stop so tight (under half an ATR) that normal noise hits it first. So I moved the plan: entry 158.76 (limit just under the 158.768 swing high, reached on a small dip), stop 158.61 (below the 158.6615 swing high that has turned price down twice, an old ceiling now acting as a floor; 0.94 ATR on the 1h chart), single target 159.00 (round number; nothing in levels.json between 158.847 and there). Risk 0.15, reward 0.24: 1.6R gross.

I tested alternatives with tools/timemachine.py (5,000 replays, 8 hours, seed 19). 158.72/158.64/158.83 gave 44% target-first at 1.375R (average +0.056R) but the stop is only 0.5 ATR and 1.375R fails the 1.5x rule; 158.72/158.62/158.83 gave 49% at 1.1R. My chosen plan family gave about 35-38% target-first, 60-64% stop-first and an average near -0.04R; history showed 12-14 targets versus 31-36 stops out of 59. Honest read: the plan now meets the 1.5R rule but the odds sit slightly under the roughly 38% break-even for 1.6R. No proven edge; the optimizer agrees (NO_EDGE).

Why still take it: the dollar is broadly up (DXY +0.7%, 10y yield 5.015%) on hot US CPI, the 1h average stack points up (EMA9 158.57 over EMA21 158.34), the event guard is CLEAR and volatility is NORMAL. Against: 1h RSI 76.4 is stretched, 5m/15m MACD histograms are slightly negative, StoneX's claim is an unverified snippet, and ING flags a Japan growth surprise. I concede these; my case is a small defined-risk dip-buy, not a high-confidence trade.
